subject: Numeracy
title: Circles, squares and triangles
objectives: Children will name circle, square and triangle.
Children will find these shapes in the classroom.
content: Circles and squares, triangles, and finding shapes around us.
teachingActivities: Handle real 3D and flat shapes; talk about sides and corners; draw shapes in the air and sand; look at shapes in the environment such as plates, windows and roofs; accept shapes in different sizes and positions.
learnerActivities: Name circle, square and triangle and find them in the classroom.
assessment: Observe whether each child names circle, square and triangle and finds them around the room.
expectedOutcomes: Finds each shape in the room.

lessons.title: Circles and squares
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will name circle and square and say how they are different.
successCriteria: Says a circle has no corners
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, compare size and length, and count.
lessons.starter: Hold up a plate and a book and say "The plate is a circle. The book is a square."
teacherActivities: Show each shape and trace the edge with a finger.
Say "A circle is round and has no corners."
Say "A square has four sides and four corners."
Play feel and name in the feely bag.
learnerActivities: Children touch the edge of a circle.
Child feels a shape and names it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each shape and trace the edge with a finger. Children: Children trace the shape.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "A circle is round and has no corners." Children: Children touch the edge of a circle.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "A square has four sides and four corners." Children: Children count the corners.
Step 4. Teacher: Play feel and name in the feely bag. Children: Child feels a shape and names it.

practical.title: Feely bag shapes
steps: Put a hand in the bag.
practical.safety: Use smooth card or wooden shapes with no sharp edges and keep them out of mouths. Supervise the bag game.

differentiation.support: Sort two shapes only and name each with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find shapes with exactly four corners.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many corners has a square?

lessons.conclusion: Put the shapes away and say circle and square.
lessons.homeConnection: Find circles and squares at home, such as plates and tiles.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name circle and square and say how they are different" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Triangles
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will name a triangle and say it has three sides and three corners.
successCriteria: Counts three sides and three corners
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, compare size and length, and count.
lessons.starter: Show a roof picture and say "This roof is a triangle. It has three sides."
teacherActivities: Show a triangle and count its three sides.
Make a triangle with three straws and playdough.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a triangle and count its three sides. Children: Children count the sides.
Step 2. Teacher: Count the three corners. Children: Children point to each corner.
Step 3. Teacher: Make a triangle with three straws and playdough. Children: Child builds a triangle.
Step 4. Teacher: Find triangles in the pictures. Children: Child points to a triangle.

practical.title: Straw triangles
practical.safety: Use short soft straws and keep them away from mouths. Wash hands after using playdough.

differentiation.support: Build the triangle together with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make triangles of different sizes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many sides has a triangle?
Where do you see a triangle?

lessons.homeConnection: Look for triangles on signs, roofs and food.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name a triangle and say it has three sides and three corners" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shapes around us
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find circles, squares and triangles around the school.
successCriteria: Finds each shape in the environment
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, compare size and length, and count.
lessons.starter: Show three shape cards and say "Today we go on a shape hunt."
teacherActivities: Show the three shape cards and say each name.
Walk around the room and look for the shapes.
Point to a shape and name it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the three shape cards and say each name. Children: Children say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Walk around the room and look for the shapes. Children: Children walk and look.
Step 3. Teacher: Point to a shape and name it. Children: Child names a shape.
Step 4. Teacher: Tally the shapes found. Children: Children count the shapes.

practical.title: Shape hunt
steps: Find a circle, square or triangle.
practical.safety: Walk slowly with an adult and keep to safe areas. Check the area before the walk.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a shape inside another shape.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Sit together and say the shape names.
lessons.homeConnection: Hunt for shapes on a walk with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find circles, squares and triangles around the school" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shape pictures
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make a picture using circles, squares and triangles.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, compare size and length, and count.
lessons.starter: Show a house made of a square, a triangle and a circle and say "I made this from shapes."
teacherActivities: Show the picture and name each shape.
Let each child choose shapes and arrange them.
Help children stick the shapes down.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the picture and name each shape. Children: Children name the shapes.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child choose shapes and arrange them. Children: Child arranges shapes.
Step 3. Teacher: Help children stick the shapes down. Children: Child sticks shapes on paper.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What did you make?" Children: Child says what they made.

practical.title: Shape house
practical.safety: Use non-toxic glue sticks and supervise so that no glue goes in mouths. Wash hands afterwards.

differentiation.support: Arrange the shapes together with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a picture with ten shapes and count each kind.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Hang the pictures and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a shape picture with paper at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a picture using circles, squares and triangles" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 shapes check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names and finds shapes.
successCriteria: Finds the shapes around the room
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, compare size and length, and count.
lessons.starter: Sing the shape song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: feely bag, shape hunt and shape pictures.
At each station ask "What shape is this?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: feely bag, shape hunt and shape pictures. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What shape is this?" Children: Child names the shape.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Shape stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use smooth shapes only. Keep glue and small items away from mouths.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two shapes.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to describe the sides and corners.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names circle; names square; names triangle; finds shapes in the environment; says sides and corners.

questions.question: How many sides has a triangle?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
Names and finds shapes with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child names and finds shapes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
